subject: Next steps: commercial path, billing preference, and security gating for Energos
message_1:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Thompson <alex.thompson@energos.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@energos.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 24 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo summary + quick procurement questions

Hi Alex / Procurement team —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and a proposed set of next steps to unblock commercial: 

- What we heard: Energos is interested in Redwood for high-throughput inference (customer-facing features). Primary gating items are procurement route (PO vs corporate card vs cloud marketplace), SOC 2 evidence for vendor risk, and a brief vendor security questionnaire.
- Immediate asks from your side: confirmation of preferred billing flow + whether marketplace procurement is an option (e.g., AWS Marketplace) and target procurement timeline from legal/finance.
- Security gating we can support quickly: we have an up-to-date SOC 2 Type II summary (attached), a standard DPA (attached) and a one-page answers doc for common vendor questionnaires. For anything deeper we can loop in our security reviewer (Monica).

Attachments: redwood_soc2_type2_summary.pdf, redwood_standard_dpa_v1.3.docx

Proposed next steps (if that works for you):
1) Alex / Procurement: confirm billing preference (PO with net30, corporate card, or marketplace listing) and whether Energos needs Redwood on a specific vendor portal.
2) If PO: share a sample PO or your PO process owner contact; we’ll route to finance.
3) If marketplace: I’ll check marketplace billing options and provide a marketplace agreement timeline.
4) Security: Alex — please confirm whether the SOC 2 summary + DPA will suffice for initial procurement (we can redline DPA on a short timeline). If you need questionnaire answers, Monica is ready to provide a 48–72 hour turnaround on standard infosec questions.

I’ll follow up tomorrow with a short mutual action plan and a proposed datesheet for procurement signoff.

Thanks,
Nikhil
--

Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo summary + quick procurement questions

Thanks Nikhil — useful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Billing preference: Procurement prefers PO (Net 30) for any new vendor > $5k MRR. We can consider corporate card for pilots under $2k.
- Marketplace: we try to use marketplace for SaaS where possible, but marketplace procurement adds an extra 2–3 weeks for onboarding and approvals — not ideal for our immediate pilot.
- Security: SOC 2 summary + DPA will usually clear initial legal review. However, our InfoSec team will still run a short vendor questionnaire (10–15 items) to confirm data flows and encryption at rest. If answers come back consistent, we can fast-track to PO routing.

Two asks for you: 
1) Can you send the DPA as a Word doc we can redline (I see it attached — thanks).
2) Provide a simple mapping of what data Redwood persists (tokens, logs, KV cache behavior) and whether we can enforce IP allowlist / VPC egress controls (this will determine whether InfoSec wants to escalate).

If you can get the questionnaire answers and the persistence mapping in 48–72 hours, I’ll try to get Procurement and Finance to queue the PO within 1 week.

-Alex

message_3:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Thompson <alex.thompson@energos.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 08:18:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Post-demo summary + quick procurement questions

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the clear asks. Quick security notes and what we can provide in a 48–72 hour window: 

- DPA: we can send a Word version and accept standard redlines for mutual obligations.
- SOC 2: attached summary covers scope (data processing and hosting in US regions), testing period (last 12 months), and control families tested. Full SOC 2 report is shared under NDA — if you need that please let me know and I’ll request it from our compliance team (turnaround 24–48 hours).
- Data persistence: Redwood by default does not retain user inputs past 30 days for hosted accounts; however for enterprise customers we offer configurable data retention, and options to disable persistent logs. KV caches are ephemeral per-session unless customer enables long-term caching. We can put this in a short mapping doc for you.
- Network controls: We support IP allowlisting for admin/API access and VPC peering for Private deployments; hosted API customers can request egress locking via partner integrations — I’ll include a quick matrix showing what’s supported today and what requires Dedicated/Private deployment.

I’ll produce: (a) DPA Word file for redlines, (b) 1-page data persistence & network controls mapping, (c) a completed answers doc to the common vendor questionnaire. Sending all within 72 hours.

Best,
Monica
--
Monica Patel
Security & Trust | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwoodinference.com

Alex
